name: Watermark Detection
description: Analyzes AI watermark and signature patterns
mechanism:
This method detects digital watermarks for video forensic authentication:

1. **Visible Watermark Detection**: The method searches for visible watermarks — logos, text overlays, station identification marks. Their presence, position, and integrity provide provenance information. Cropping or overlaying to remove watermarks indicates potential manipulation intent.

2. **Invisible Watermark Extraction**: Robust invisible watermarks embedded in the frequency domain (DCT, DWT coefficients) or spatial domain are extracted. Common watermarking standards (Digimarc, BWARN) are tested. Intact watermarks verify content authenticity; corrupted watermarks indicate post-watermark manipulation.

3. **C2PA/Content Credentials Detection**: Modern content authenticity standards (Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity) embed cryptographically signed provenance metadata. The method checks for C2PA manifests and verifies digital signatures, providing chain-of-custody information for the content.

4. **Watermark Consistency Analysis**: If watermarks are present, they should be consistent across all frames. The method checks temporal watermark stability — partial watermark removal (only in the deepfaked face region) or watermark corruption in specific frames indicates selective manipulation.

5. **AI-Generated Content Watermark**: Some AI generators embed their own watermarks (SynthID by Google, DALL-E metadata). The method searches for known AI generator watermarks. Detection of an AI generator watermark provides direct evidence of synthetic content generation.
parameters:
Analysis type: metadata
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through watermark detection analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video
